   101	    (⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)) ≤
   102	      ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) k) ⊓ V) := by
   103	  refine le_iInf fun k => ?_
   104	  refine Fin.cases ?_ ?_ k
   105	  · rw [Fin.cons_zero]
   106	    exact le_trans (restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ) (le_inf hiV le_rfl)
   107	  · intro j
   108	    rw [Fin.cons_succ]
   109	    exact iInf_le _ j

   111	/-- Prepending `i_fix` to the empty tuple yields an intersection containing `V`
   112	(the augmentation node case). -/
   113	private lemma le_restrictedIntersection_cons_empty (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   114	    (σ : Fin 0 → 𝒰.I₀) :
   115	    V ≤ ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀) k) ⊓ V) := by
   116	  refine le_iInf fun k => ?_
   117	  rw [Fin.fin_one_eq_zero k, Fin.cons_zero]
   118	  exact le_inf hiV le_rfl

   120	/-- The open underlying the level-`m` contracting-homotopy coefficient: level `0` is `V` (the
   121	augmentation node), level `m+1` is the restricted intersection `⨅ₖ (U_{σ k} ⊓ V)`. -/
   122	private def homotopyOpen : (m : ℕ) → (Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) → TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X
   123	  | 0, _ => V
   124	  | _ + 1, σ => ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)

   126	/-- The coface inclusion of the contracting-homotopy opens. -/
   127	private lemma homotopyOpen_le_coface : ∀ {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (j : Fin (m + 1)),
   128	    homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) σ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m (σ ∘ j.succAbove)
   129	  | 0, σ, _ => restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ
   130	  | _ + 1, _, j => le_iInf fun l => iInf_le _ (j.succAbove l)
   131	
   132	/-- The prepend inclusion of the contracting-homotopy opens (prepending `i_fix` does not shrink the
   133	open, because `V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix`). -/
   134	private lemma homotopyOpen_le_prepend (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) :
   135	    ∀ {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀),
   136	      homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m σ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ)
   137	  | 0, σ => le_restrictedIntersection_cons_empty 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ
   138	  | _ + 1, σ => restrictedIntersection_le_cons 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ
   139	
   140	/-- Dependent coefficient family for the contracting-homotopy engine: the sections of `F` over
   141	`homotopyOpen m σ`.  Kept as a reducible abbreviation so the `AddCommGroup` instance is the
   142	generic one on `Ab`-objects (no bespoke match-instance). -/
   143	noncomputable abbrev cechSectionCoeff (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) : Type u :=
   144	  ToType (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj
   145	    (Opposite.op (homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m σ)))
   146	
   147	/-- The engine coface maps: presheaf face restrictions (level `0 → 1` is the augmentation
   148	restriction `Γ(V) → Γ(U'_σ)`). -/
   149	noncomputable def cechSectionCoface (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀)
   150	    (j : Fin (m + 1)) :
   151	    cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V m (σ ∘ j.succAbove) →+ cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) σ :=
   152	  ConcreteCategory.hom (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   153	    (homOfLE (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ j)).op)
   154	
   155	/-- The engine prepend maps: genuine restrictions (level `1 → 0` is the restriction
   156	`Γ(U'_{(i_fix)}) → Γ(V)` along `V ≤ U'_{i_fix}`). -/
   157	noncomputable def cechSectionPrepend (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀)
   158	    (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) :
   159	    cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) →+ cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V m σ :=
   160	  ConcreteCategory.hom (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   161	    (homOfLE (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ)).op)
   162	
   163	/-- Transport of a Čech coefficient along an equality of index tuples is the canonical
   164	restriction between the (equal) intersection opens. -/
   165	private lemma cechSectionCoeff_transport {m : ℕ} {τ₁ τ₂ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀}
   166	    (h : τ₁ = τ₂)
   167	    (hle : homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) τ₂ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) τ₁)
   168	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) τ₁) :
   169	    (h ▸ y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) τ₂)
   170	      = ConcreteCategory.hom
   171	          (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map (homOfLE hle).op)
   172	          y := by
   173	  subst h
   174	  rw [show homOfLE hle = 𝟙 _ from Subsingleton.elim _ _, op_id,
   175	    CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]
   176	  rfl
   177	
   178	/-- Unit compatibility `hu` for the contracting-homotopy engine: deleting the prepended
   179	`i_fix` and then applying the prepend restriction is the identity transport (both sides are
   180	restriction chains between the same opens). -/
   181	lemma cechSection_hu (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   182	    {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀)
   183	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1)
   184	      ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (0 : Fin (m + 2)).succAbove)) :
   185	    cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (m + 1) σ
   186	        (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) 0 y)
   187	      = (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ) ▸ y := by
   188	  rw [cechSectionCoeff_transport 𝒰 F V (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ)
   189	    (le_of_eq (by rw [CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ]))]
   190	  exact (restriction_comp_apply _ _ _ y).trans (restriction_eq_of_parallel _ _ _ y)
   191	
   192	/-- Shift compatibility `hsh` for the contracting-homotopy engine: prepend commutes with the later
   193	cofaces (both sides are restriction chains between the same opens). -/
   194	lemma cechSection_hsh (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   195	    {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (k : Fin (m + 1))
   196	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1)
   197	      ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove)) :
   198	    cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (m + 1) σ
   199	        (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) k.succ y)
   200	      = cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V m σ k
   201	          (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV m (σ ∘ k.succAbove)
   202	            ((CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k) ▸ y)) := by
   203	  have hle : homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix (σ ∘ k.succAbove)) ≤
   204	      homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove) :=
   205	    le_of_eq (by rw [CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k])
   206	  rw [cechSectionCoeff_transport 𝒰 F V
   207	    (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k) hle]
   208	  refine Eq.trans (restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ)
   209	    (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V (Fin.cons i_fix σ) k.succ) y) ?_
   210	  refine Eq.trans (restriction_eq_of_parallel _ _ (homOfLE ((homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ k).trans
   211	    ((homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)).trans hle))).op y) ?_
   212	  refine Eq.symm ?_
   213	  refine Eq.trans (DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V m σ k)
   214	    (restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)) hle y)) ?_
   215	  exact restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ k)
   216	    ((homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)).trans hle) y
   217	
   218	end RestrictionEngine

   220	/-! ### Degree-0 augmentation seam — helper bricks for `sectionCechAugV_π`.
   221	
   222	The seam unwinds `sectionCechAugV ≫ Pi.π σ` through the proved Base seams.  The Čech
   223	augmentation composed with the push–pull of *any* `Over X`-morphism `g : Y ⟶ Y₀` into the
   224	backbone collapses — through the terminal object `Over.mk (𝟙 X)` of `Over X` — to the
   225	pullback–pushforward adjunction unit at `Y.hom` (`cechAugmentation_pushPullMap`); the unit, in
   226	turn, reads through the per-leg section identification `pushPull_leg_sections` as the plain
   227	presheaf restriction (`unit_pushPull_leg_sections`), because it is conjugate via
   228	`Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq` to the restriction adjunction whose unit *is* the restriction on
   229	sections (`Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app`). -/
   230	
   231	section AugSeam
   232	
   233	/-- An `eqToHom` between section groups of an abelian presheaf over (propositionally) equal
   234	opens is the presheaf restriction along the induced inclusion.  Transport-killer for the
   235	augmentation seam. -/
   236	private lemma eqToHom_eq_restriction (P : (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u})
   237	    {A B : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X} (hAB : A = B) (hle : B ≤ A)
   238	    (h : P.obj (Opposite.op A) = P.obj (Opposite.op B)) :
   239	    eqToHom h = P.map (homOfLE hle).op := by
   240	  subst hAB
   241	  refine Eq.trans (eqToHom_refl _ h) ?_
   242	  refine Eq.trans (P.map_id (Opposite.op A)).symm ?_
   243	  exact congrArg P.map (congrArg Quiver.Hom.op (Subsingleton.elim (𝟙 A) (homOfLE hle)))
   244	
   245	/-- Precomposing the scheme-level push–pull comparison `rawPushPullMap` with the
   246	pullback–pushforward adjunction unit at the source structure map yields the unit at the
   247	target structure map (`η^{p₁} ≫ G(a) = η^{p₂}`, the mate-calculus collapse of the degree-`0`
   248	augmentation leg). -/
   249	private lemma rawPushPullMap_unit {Z₁ Z₂ : Scheme.{u}} (a : Z₂ ⟶ Z₁)
   250	    (p₁ : Z₁ ⟶ X) (p₂ : Z₂ ⟶ X) (w : a ≫ p₁ = p₂) (F : X.Modules) :
   251	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction p₁).unit.app F ≫
   252	        rawPushPullMap a p₁ p₂ w F =
   253	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction p₂).unit.app F := by
   254	  subst w
   255	  rw [rawPushPullMap_self, pushPull_unit_comp a p₁ F]
   256	  refine congrArg (fun m =>
   257	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction p₁).unit.app F ≫ m) ?_
   258	  refine Eq.trans ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward p₁).map_comp _ _) ?_
   259	  refine congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.pushforward p₁).map
   260	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction a).unit.app
   261	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback p₁).obj F)) ≫ m) ?_
   262	  -- `pushforward` is strict: `p₁_*(a_* χ) = (pushforwardComp).hom ≫ (a ≫ p₁)_* χ`
   263	  -- (the comparison cell is the identity on sections).
   264	  apply Scheme.Modules.hom_ext
   265	  intro U
   266	  rfl
   267	
   268	/-- The inverse of the Čech-nerve point identification is the pullback–pushforward
   269	adjunction unit of the identity morphism. -/
   270	private lemma cechNervePointIso_inv_eq_unit (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules) :
   271	    (cechNervePointIso 𝒰 F).inv =
   272	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F := by
   273	  have star := unit_conjugateEquiv (Adjunction.id (C := X.Modules))
   274	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)) (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).hom F
   275	  rw [Scheme.Modules.conjugateEquiv_pullbackId_hom] at star
   276	  simp only [Adjunction.id_unit, NatTrans.id_app, Functor.id_obj] at star
   277	  have star2 : (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardId X).inv.app F =
   278	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫
   279	        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).hom.app F) :=
   280	    (Category.id_comp _).symm.trans star
   281	  have hnat := (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardId X).inv.naturality
   282	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).inv.app F)
   283	  simp only [Functor.id_obj, Functor.id_map] at hnat
   284	  refine Eq.trans (hnat : (cechNervePointIso 𝒰 F).inv = _) ?_
   285	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map
   286	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).inv.app F)) star2) ?_
   287	  refine Eq.trans (Category.assoc _ _ _) ?_
   288	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m =>
   289	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫ m)
   290	    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map_comp _ _).symm)) ?_
   291	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m =>
   292	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫
   293	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map m) (Iso.hom_inv_id_app _ _)) ?_
   294	  exact (congrArg (fun m =>
   295	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫ m)
   296	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map_id _)).trans (Category.comp_id _)
   297	
   298	/-- The Čech augmentation composed with the push–pull of *any* `Over X`-morphism into the
   299	degree-`0` backbone is the pullback–pushforward adjunction unit at the structure map: the
   300	composite `Y ⟶ Y₀ ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 X)` is a morphism into the terminal object, so the
   301	augmentation leg needs no unwinding. -/
   302	private lemma cechAugmentation_pushPullMap (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules)
   303	    {Y : Over X}
   304	    (g : Y ⟶ (coverCechNerveOver 𝒰).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) :
   305	    cechAugmentation 𝒰 F ≫ pushPullMap F g =
   306	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction Y.hom).unit.app F := by
   307	  have happ : (CechNerve 𝒰 F).hom.app (SimplexCategory.mk 0) =
   308	      pushPullMap F
   309	        ((coverCechNerveOverAug 𝒰).hom.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) :=
   310	    Eq.trans rfl (Category.id_comp _)
   311	  rw [cechAugmentation, Category.assoc]
   312	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (cechNervePointIso 𝒰 F).inv ≫ m)
   313	    (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫ pushPullMap F g) happ)
   314	      ((pushPullMap_comp F _ g).symm))) ?_
   315	  rw [cechNervePointIso_inv_eq_unit, pushPullMap_eq_raw]
   316	  exact rawPushPullMap_unit _ _ _ _ F
   317	
   318	/-- The pullback–pushforward unit reads through the per-leg section identification as the
   319	plain `F`-restriction `Γ(V, F) → Γ(U_σ ∩ V, F)`. -/
   320	private lemma unit_pushPull_leg_sections (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (F : X.Modules)
   321	    {p : ℕ} (σ : Fin (p + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) :
   322	    (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   323	        (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   324	          (Opposite.op V)).map
   325	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   326	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F) ≫
   327	      (pushPull_leg_sections 𝒰 F σ V).hom =
   328	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   329	      (homOfLE (inf_le_right : coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ ⊓ V ≤ V)).op := by
   330	  have hW : Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) ''ᵁ
   331	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) ⁻¹ᵁ V) = coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ ⊓ V := by
   332	    rw [Scheme.Hom.image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf, Scheme.Opens.opensRange_ι]
   333	  -- (i) the leg iso, with its `eqToHom` transport canonicalised to the `congrArg` form
   334	  -- (definitional: projections of `Iso.trans`/`eqToIso` plus proof irrelevance)
   335	  have hdec : (pushPull_leg_sections 𝒰 F σ V).hom =
   336	      (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   337	          (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   338	            (Opposite.op V)).map
   339	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   340	          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   341	            (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).inv.app F)) ≫
   342	      eqToHom (congrArg
   343	        (fun W => ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op W))
   344	        hW) := rfl
   345	  -- (ii) the pullback unit is conjugate to the restriction unit via `leftAdjointUniq`
   346	  -- (`restrictFunctorIsoPullback` *is* the `leftAdjointUniq` iso, definitionally)
   347	  have hLAU : (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   348	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫
   349	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   350	        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   351	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).inv.app F) =
   352	      (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   353	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F := by
   354	    have h0 : (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   355	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫
   356	        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   357	          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   358	            (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).hom.app F) =
   359	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   360	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F :=
   361	      Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app _ _ F
   362	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫
   363	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   364	        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   365	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).inv.app F)) h0.symm) ?_
   366	    refine Eq.trans (Category.assoc _ _ _) ?_
   367	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   368	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫ m)
   369	      (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map_comp
   370	        _ _).symm)) ?_
   371	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   372	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫
   373	        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map m)
   374	      (Iso.hom_inv_id_app _ _)) ?_
   375	    exact (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   376	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫ m)
   377	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map_id _)).trans
   378	      (Category.comp_id _)
   379	  -- (iii) the restriction unit on sections is the plain restriction (definitional,
   380	  -- `Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app`)
   381	  have hunit : (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   382	        (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   383	          (Opposite.op V)).map
   384	      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   385	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F) =
   386	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   387	      (homOfLE ((Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ)).image_preimage_le V)).op := rfl
   388	  -- assemble: fuse the unit with the comparison leg, read off the restriction, and
   389	  -- collapse the two parallel restriction chains (term-chained: `rw` cannot re-match
   390	  -- composites whose stored middle objects are defeq-but-not-syntactic).
   391	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   392	      (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   393	        (Opposite.op V)).map
   394	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction

3940	\label{sec:grassmannian_scheme}

3942	The Quot construction proceeds by embedding \(\Quot^{\Phi,L}_{E/X/S}\) as a
3943	locally closed subfunctor of a Grassmannian over \(S\). Since Mathlib carries
3944	no Grassmannian \emph{scheme} (only a finite-rank-quotient variety in
3945	linear algebra), we package the construction here.

81	  \textit{Source: [Nitsure], \S 1 (FGA Explained Ch.~5); cf.\ [Hartshorne],

83	  Let \(X \to S\) be a finite-type morphism of noetherian schemes and let \(L\)
84	  be a line bundle on \(X\). For a coherent sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(X\) whose
85	  schematic support is proper over \(S\) and a point \(s \in S\), write \(X_s\)

90	  \(m \gg 0\), with the graded Hilbert function

- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.

# Quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine are sections-tilde (Stacks 01HV/01I8)

Project-local: the affine quasi-coherent structure theorem.  For an `𝒪_X`-module `F`
on an affine `X = Spec R`, with `M = Γ(X, F)`, there is a natural isomorphism
`F ≅ M^~`, under which `Γ(D(f), F) = M_f`.

## The Mathlib gradient

Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Tilde` development provides:

* `Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓ F : tilde (Γ F) ⟶ F` — the counit of the
  tilde ⊣ global-sections adjunction;
* `isIso_fromTildeΓ_iff : IsIso F.fromTildeΓ ↔ (tilde.functor R).essImage F`;
* `isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_presentation F (P : F.Presentation) : IsIso F.fromTildeΓ` —
  the counit is an isomorphism whenever `F` admits a **global** presentation
  (a global generating family together with a global generating family of relations).

The genuine remaining gap — **Stacks Tag 01I8**, the affine equivalence
`QCoh(Spec R) ≃ Mod R` — is the implication

  `[IsQuasicoherent F]  ⟹  IsIso F.fromTildeΓ`   (on the affine `Spec R`).

`IsQuasicoherent F` only supplies *local* presentation data on a cover
(`QuasicoherentData`); turning that into a *global* presentation on the affine base
(or directly into membership of the essential image of `tilde`) is the content of the
affine equivalence and is not yet in Mathlib.  See the `## Handoff` section at the
bottom of this file for the precise decomposition.

This file therefore delivers the structure theorem **conditioned on the counit being
an isomorphism** (`qcoh_iso_tilde_sections`), and a ready-to-use **presentation form**
(`qcoh_iso_tilde_sections_of_presentation`) that discharges that condition via the
Mathlib presentation lemma.  Once the 01I8 instance
`[IsQuasicoherent F] → IsIso F.fromTildeΓ` lands, the conditional form upgrades to the
unconditional quasi-coherent statement with no further work.
-/

/-! ## Handoff — closing the 01I8 gap

The unconditional quasi-coherent statement

```
theorem qcoh_iso_tilde_sections_qcoh (F : (Spec R).Modules) [IsQuasicoherent F] :
    F ≅ tilde (moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj F)
```

is obtained from `qcoh_iso_tilde_sections` the instant the following instance is available:

```
instance (F : (Spec R).Modules) [IsQuasicoherent F] : IsIso F.fromTildeΓ
```

equivalently (by `isIso_fromTildeΓ_iff`) `(tilde.functor R).essImage F`, equivalently a
**global** `F.Presentation` (fed to `qcoh_iso_tilde_sections_of_presentation`).

The needed Mathlib-gradient sub-steps (all on the affine base `Spec R`):

1. `IsQuasicoherent F` ⟹ `F` is generated by global sections: produce
   `F.GeneratingSections` (a global epi `free I ⟶ F`).  On `Spec R` this is the affine
   global-generation statement (Hartshorne II.5.16 / Stacks 01I8); `QuasicoherentData`
   only gives generation locally on a basic-open cover, which must be globalised using
   `PrimeSpectrum.exists_idempotent_basicOpen_eq_of_isClopen`-style partition-of-unity /
   the compactness of `Spec R` and the localisation-of-sections property of qcoh sheaves.
   **This is the single genuine remaining blocker** (sections of qcoh `F` over `D(f)`
   localise — `Γ(D(f), F) = Γ(X, F)_f`, Stacks 01HV(4)/01I8 — is itself absent from Mathlib:
   `grep` confirms the only `IsQuasicoherent` content in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/` is
   `Modules/Tilde.lean`, with no localisation-of-sections and no abelian-subcategory closure).
2. The kernel of `free I ⟶ F` is again quasi-coherent on `Spec R` (NB: not yet a Mathlib
   instance — `kernel σ.π` is not automatically qcoh; this needs the qcoh-is-abelian-subcategory
   fact, itself downstream of step 1's local structure), hence again globally generated by
   step 1; this yields the two `GeneratingSections` `σ`, `τ` of `F.Presentation`.
3. Feed those two generating families to `isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_genSections` (below), which
   bundles them into `F.Presentation` and applies Mathlib's `isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_presentation`,
   producing the `IsIso F.fromTildeΓ` instance above.

**Steps 2–3 are now formalised** as the axiom-clean `isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_genSections` and
`qcoh_iso_tilde_sections_of_genSections` (the structure theorem directly from the two generating
families), with `free_isQuasicoherent` recording that free coefficient sheaves are qcoh.  Step 1 —
the load-bearing ~few-hundred-LOC affine global-generation / localisation-of-sections input — is
the single genuine mathematical blocker; once it supplies `σ : F.GeneratingSections` and
`τ : (kernel σ.π).GeneratingSections` for a quasi-coherent `F`, the instance and the unconditional
upgrade of `qcoh_iso_tilde_sections` follow with no further work.

/-- Per-leg coherence (replica of the Base `private pushPull_binary_leg_coherence` for a
general ambient open immersion): the push–pull map of an over-morphism `Over.homMk c` is,
through the canonical leg iso, the pushforward of the restriction unit. -/
private lemma pushPull_leg_coherence {A C' : Scheme.{u}} (q : A ⟶ X)
    (c : C' ⟶ A) [IsOpenImmersion c] (pC : C' ⟶ X) (wC : c ≫ q = pC) (F : X.Modules) :
    pushPullMap F (Over.homMk c wC : Over.mk pC ⟶ Over.mk q) =
      (pushforward q).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction c).unit.app
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback q).obj F)) ≫
        (pushPullLegIso q c pC wC F).hom := by
  have hraw : pushPullMap F (Over.homMk c wC : Over.mk pC ⟶ Over.mk q)
      = rawPushPullMap c q pC wC F := rfl
  rw [hraw, rawPushPullMap_self_gen]
  have hLAU : (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction c).unit.app
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback q).obj F) ≫
        (pushforward c).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback c).hom.app
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback q).obj F)) =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction c).unit.app
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback q).obj F) :=
    Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app _ _ _
  subst wC
  simp only [pushPullLegIso, Iso.trans_hom, Functor.mapIso_hom, eqToIso.hom,
    Iso.app_hom, Category.comp_id,
    Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr, eqToIso_refl, Iso.refl_hom, NatTrans.id_app]
  rw [← hLAU]
  simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]

  open immersion preserves quasi-coherence

  quasi-coherent module on the affine scheme \(\Spec\Gamma(X,V)\); by the
  affine structure theorem (Stacks 01I8, Lean
  \texttt{isIso\_fromTildeΓ\_of\_isQuasicoherent}) the tilde--\(\Gamma\)
  counit \(\widetilde{\Gamma(G,\top)} \to G\) is an isomorphism.

  (the \(V\)-sections of the pullback--pushforward adjunction unit followed by
  restriction along \(\top \le j^{-1}V\)) is bijective. Indeed the two

  \emph{equality} of opens \(j(j^{-1}V) = V\), hence bijective; the component

  the equality \(\top = j^{-1}V\). Thus \(b\) is a composite of three
  bijections.

  \(\Gamma(X,V)\)-action on \(\Gamma(G,\top)\) being through the canonical

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, hold a 1-to-1 correspondence with the Lean, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. Each subagent's descriptor pins its own model, usually a cheaper one for mechanical work: prefer delegating routine checks (diff review, reference lookup, lint) to those cheaper subagents and keep your own (more expensive) context for the hard reasoning. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

private lemma res_res (M : X.Modules) {A B C : X.Opens} (hBA : B ≤ A) (hCB : C ≤ B)
    (hCA : C ≤ A) (x : Γ(M, A)) :
    M.presheaf.map (homOfLE hCB).op (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE hBA).op x)

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme.Modules

variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}

-- local copies of the composition helpers (private in QuotScheme.lean)
private lemma res_res' (N : Y.Modules) {A B C : Y.Opens} (hBA : B ≤ A) (hCB : C ≤ B)
    (hCA : C ≤ A) (x : Γ(N, A)) :
    N.presheaf.map (homOfLE hCB).op (N.presheaf.map (homOfLE hBA).op x)
      = N.presheaf.map (homOfLE hCA).op x := by
  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp]
  rfl

private lemma res_self' (N : Y.Modules) {A : Y.Opens} (x : Γ(N, A)) :
    N.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_rfl : A ≤ A)).op x = x := by
  rw [Subsingleton.elim (homOfLE (le_rfl : A ≤ A)) (𝟙 A), op_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]
  rfl

/-- Additive section transport across an equality of opens, by mutual restriction. -/
private def resAddEquivOfEq (N : Y.Modules) {A B : Y.Opens} (h : A = B) :
    Γ(N, A) ≃+ Γ(N, B) where
  toFun := N.presheaf.map (homOfLE h.ge).op
  invFun := N.presheaf.map (homOfLE h.le).op
  left_inv x := by rw [res_res' N h.ge h.le le_rfl, res_self' N x]
  right_inv x := by rw [res_res' N h.le h.ge le_rfl, res_self' N x]
  map_add' := map_add _

/-- **Converse transport: section localization on the ambient scheme forces the P1 datum.**
For an affine open `U ⊆ Y` with `j = hU.fromSpec` and a sheaf of modules `N` on `Y`, if for
every `f' : Γ(Y, U)` the section restriction `Γ(N, U) → Γ(N, D(f'))` is
`IsLocalizedModule (powers f')` over `Γ(Y, U)`, then the tilde–Γ counit of the pullback
`j^* N` is an isomorphism. This is the reverse of the gap2 chain
(`section_localization_hfr_aux_general` + `isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_hP1` run backwards):
the `gammaPullbackImageIso` section comparisons and the `fromSpec` open identifications
(`fromSpec_image_basicOpen`, `image_top = U`) transport the localization to the `Spec`-side
sections, where the affine engine `isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isLocalizedModule_restrict` applies.
Project-local. -/
theorem isIso_fromTildeΓ_pullback_fromSpec_of_isLocalizedModule
    (N : Y.Modules) {U : Y.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (H : ∀ f' : Γ(Y, U),
      ∀ [Module Γ(Y, U) Γ(N, Y.basicOpen f')]
        [IsScalarTower Γ(Y, U) Γ(Y, Y.basicOpen f') Γ(N, Y.basicOpen f')],
      IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f') (restrictBasicOpenₗ N f')) :
    IsIso (Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓ
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback hU.fromSpec).obj N)) := by
  set j := hU.fromSpec with hj
  apply isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isLocalizedModule_restrict
  intro f'
  set M' := (Scheme.Modules.pullback j).obj N with hM'
  have eT : (j ''ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec Γ(Y, U)).Opens)) = U :=
    (Scheme.Hom.image_top_eq_opensRange j).trans hU.opensRange_fromSpec
  have eB : (j ''ᵁ (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f')) = Y.basicOpen f' :=
    hU.fromSpec_image_basicOpen f'
  -- module instances on the ambient side
  letI : Module Γ(Y, U) Γ(N, Y.basicOpen f') :=
    Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(Y, U) Γ(Y, Y.basicOpen f'))
  haveI : IsScalarTower Γ(Y, U) Γ(Y, Y.basicOpen f') Γ(N, Y.basicOpen f') :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul (fun _ _ => rfl)
  haveI hloc := H f'
  -- the additive section comparisons
  let E₁ : ToType Γ(N, U) ≃+
      ToType ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M').presheaf.obj (.op ⊤)) :=
    ((resAddEquivOfEq N eT.symm).trans
      (gammaPullbackImageIso j N ⊤).addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv.symm)
  let E₂ : ToType Γ(N, Y.basicOpen f') ≃+
      ToType ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M').presheaf.obj (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f'))) :=
    ((resAddEquivOfEq N eB.symm).trans
      (gammaPullbackImageIso j N (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f')).addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv.symm)
  -- the Spec-side restriction, R-linearly
  let h : ToType ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M').presheaf.obj (.op ⊤))
      →ₗ[Γ(Y, U)]
        ToType ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M').presheaf.obj (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f'))) :=
    ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M').presheaf.map
      (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f' ≤ ⊤)).op).hom
  -- semilinearity (over the identity of `Γ(Y, U)`)
  have he₁ : ∀ (a : Γ(Y, U)) (x : ToType Γ(N, U)),
      E₁ (a • x) = a • E₁ x := by
    sorry
  have he₂ : ∀ (a : Γ(Y, U)) (x : ToType Γ(N, Y.basicOpen f')),
      E₂ (a • x) = a • E₂ x := by
    sorry
  -- intertwining
  have hh : ∀ x, h (E₁ x) = E₂ (restrictBasicOpenₗ N f' x) := by
    sorry
  have RESULT : IsLocalizedModule
      ((Submonoid.powers f').map ((RingEquiv.refl Γ(Y, U)) : Γ(Y, U) →+* Γ(Y, U))) h :=
    isLocalizedModule_of_ringEquiv_semilinear (RingEquiv.refl Γ(Y, U))
      (Submonoid.powers f') (restrictBasicOpenₗ N f') E₁ E₂ he₁ he₂ h hh
  have key : (Submonoid.powers f').map ((RingEquiv.refl Γ(Y, U)) : Γ(Y, U) →+* Γ(Y, U))
      = Submonoid.powers f' := by
    rw [Submonoid.map_powers]
    rfl
  rw [key] at RESULT
  exact RESULT

end Scheme.Modules

end AlgebraicGeometry

Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) and secrets are excluded/blocked
  automatically, so a broad add still won't commit them.
- If the `pre-commit` guard ever reports *"possible secret in staged changes"* and
  your own diff is clean, you have staged more than you meant to — commit with
  `-- <paths>` rather than setting `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`, which only
  silences the guard and still commits everything staged.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).

  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

1	\chapter{Milne Theorem 3.2: Rational maps into abelian varieties}
     2	\label{chap:Albanese_Thm32RationalMapExtension}
     3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean
     4	
     5	\section{Setup and statement}
     6	\label{sec:thm32_setup}
     7	
     8	Fix an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\), a nonsingular variety \(X\) over
     9	\(\bar k\), and an abelian variety \(A\) over \(\bar k\).  Thus \(X\) is
    10	integral and smooth, while \(A\) is a complete smooth group variety.  A
    11	rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow A\) is represented by a regular
    12	morphism \(\varphi_U \colon U \to A\) on a dense open subset
    13	\(U \subseteq X\), two such pairs \((U, \varphi_U)\) and \((U', \varphi_{U'})\) being equivalent
    14	if \(\varphi_U\) and \(\varphi_{U'}\) agree on \(U \cap U'\).
    15	
    16	\begin{theorem}
    17	\leanok
    18	[Milne Theorem~3.2: a rational map from a nonsingular variety to an abelian variety extends]
    19	  \label{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends}
    20	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av}
    21	  \uses{thm:codim_one_extension, lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy, lem:av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty}
    22	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0023}
    23	
    24	  Let \(X\) be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\), let \(A\) be
    25	  an abelian variety over \(\bar k\), and let \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow A\) be a rational
    26	  map. Then \(f\) is defined on the whole of \(X\): there is a unique regular morphism
    27	  \(\widetilde f \colon X \to A\) whose restriction to some (equivalently, every) dense open
    28	  set of definition \(U \subseteq X\) of \(f\) agrees with \(\varphi_U\).
    29	\end{theorem}
    30	
    31	\begin{proof}
    32	  Let \(U\) be the maximal open subset on which \(f\) is defined, and put
    33	  \(Z=X\setminus U\).  Since a nonsingular variety is normal and \(A\) is
    34	  complete, \cref{thm:codim_one_extension} shows that every point of \(Z\)
    35	  has codimension at least two.  On the other hand,
    36	  \cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy} says that, for a rational map into a
    37	  group variety, \(Z\) is either empty or pure of codimension one.  The
    38	  second alternative is incompatible with the first conclusion, so
    39	  \(Z=\varnothing\).  Hence \(U=X\), and the representative of \(f\) on
    40	  \(U\) is the desired morphism \(\widetilde f\colon X\to A\).
    41	
    42	  If two morphisms \(X\to A\) represent \(f\), they agree on a dense open
    43	  subset of \(X\).  Their equalizer is closed because \(A\) is separated,
    44	  and it contains that dense open subset.  Since \(X\) is reduced, the two
    45	  morphisms are equal.  Thus the extension is unique.
    46	\end{proof}
    47	
    48	\begin{remark}
    49	  \label{rmk:thm32_role_of_ab}
    50	  The Auslander--Buchsbaum theorem is not needed for
    51	  \cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends}.  The codimension-one argument uses
    52	  regularity only to obtain normality and discrete valuation rings at prime
    53	  divisors; properness then supplies extensions by the valuative criterion.
    54	  It does not extend across a codimension-two locus by a depth argument.
    55	  The stronger Cohen--Macaulay consequences of Auslander--Buchsbaum in
    56	  \cref{chap:Albanese_AuslanderBuchsbaum} describe the same regular local
    57	  rings but are logically separate from Milne's proof.
    58	\end{remark}
    59	
    60	\section{Why the proof is characteristic-free}
    61	\label{sec:thm32_char_free}
    62	
    63	Both ingredients are independent of the characteristic:
    64	\begin{itemize}
    65	  \item \emph{Theorem~3.1 / codim-\(\geq 2\) extension} (\cref{thm:codim_one_extension}):
    66	    a codimension-one local ring on a normal variety is a discrete valuation
    67	    ring, and the valuative criterion of properness extends the map over that
    68	    local ring.
    69	  \item \emph{Lemma~3.3 / pure-codim-\(1\) indeterminacy for maps into a group variety}
    70	    (\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}): Milne's proof forms the difference map
    71	    \(\Phi(x, y) := \varphi(x)\,\varphi(y)^{-1} \colon X \times X \dashrightarrow A\) and
    72	    examines its pole divisors along the diagonal.  This uses the group law,
    73	    regularity, and the codimension-one support of principal divisors, none
    74	    of which imposes a characteristic restriction.
    75	\end{itemize}
    76	Consequently \cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends} holds over every algebraically closed
    77	field, in arbitrary characteristic.
    78	
    79	\section{Application to the symmetric-product Albanese map}
    80	\label{sec:thm32_application_to_a4d}
    81	
    82	Let \(C\) be a complete nonsingular curve of genus \(g>0\), let \(J\) be
    83	its Jacobian, and let \(\varphi\colon C\to A\) send a chosen point \(P\) to
    84	zero.  The symmetric map
    85	\[
    86	  (P_1,\ldots,P_g)\longmapsto
    87	  \varphi(P_1)+\cdots+\varphi(P_g)
    88	\]
    89	descends to a morphism \(\varphi^{(g)}\colon C^{(g)}\to A\).  The
    90	Abel--Jacobi morphism \(C^{(g)}\to J\) is birational, so composing
    91	\(\varphi^{(g)}\) with its rational inverse gives a rational map
    92	\(J\dashrightarrow A\).  Since \(J\) is nonsingular,
    93	\cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends} makes this map regular.  It factors
    94	\(\varphi\) through \(C\to J\), and the rigidity theorem shows that it is a
    95	homomorphism.  This is the existence step in the Albanese universal property
    96	of \(J\) proved in \cref{chap:Albanese_AlbaneseUP}.
    97	
    98	\section{Structure of the proof}
    99	\label{sec:thm32_lean_encoding}
   100	
   101	The argument separates into three elementary reductions.  Smoothness makes
   102	the abelian variety reduced; geometric irreducibility then makes it
   103	integral.  Milne's two indeterminacy results force the indeterminacy locus to
   104	be empty.  Finally, a rational map with empty indeterminacy locus has a
   105	global representative, unique because its source is reduced and its target
   106	is separated.
   107	
   108	\section{Auxiliary lemmas}
   109	\label{sec:thm32_lean_helpers}
   110	
   111	We record the reductions concerning the target and the indeterminacy locus.
   112	
   113	\begin{lemma}\leanok
   114	[A scheme smooth over a field is reduced]
   115	  \label{lem:isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}
   116	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}
   117	  Let \(A\) be a scheme over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\).  If
   118	  the structure morphism \(A\to\Spec\bar k\) is smooth, then \(A\) is
   119	  reduced.
   120	\end{lemma}
   121	\begin{proof}
   122	  An algebraically closed field is perfect.  A scheme smooth over a
   123	  perfect field is regular, since its local rings are geometrically
   124	  regular over the field.  Regular local rings are reduced, and
   125	  reducedness is local; hence \(A\) is reduced.
   126	\end{proof}
   127	
   128	\begin{lemma}\leanok
   129	[Integrality of the abelian variety]
   130	  \label{lem:av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred}
   131	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred}
   132	  \uses{lem:isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}
   133	  An abelian variety \(A\) over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\) is
   134	  integral.  Indeed, it is geometrically irreducible and smooth over
   135	  \(\bar k\), hence irreducible and reduced.
   136	\end{lemma}
   137	\begin{proof}
   138	  The spectrum of \(\bar k\) consists of one point.  Geometric
   139	  irreducibility of the structure morphism therefore implies that the
   140	  underlying topological space of \(A\) is irreducible.  By
   141	  \cref{lem:isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}, \(A\) is also reduced.  A
   142	  nonempty scheme is integral precisely when it is irreducible and
   143	  reduced, so \(A\) is integral.
   144	\end{proof}
   145	
   146	\begin{lemma}\leanok
   147	[Emptiness of the indeterminacy locus of a rational map into an abelian variety]
   148	  \label{lem:av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty}
   149	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty}
   150	  \uses{lem:av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred, lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy, thm:codim_one_extension}
   151	  For a rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow A\) from a nonsingular variety
   152	  \(X\) to an abelian variety \(A\) over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\),
   153	  the indeterminacy locus \(Z(f)\) is empty.
   154	\end{lemma}
   155	\begin{proof}
   156	  The abelian variety \(A\) is integral
   157	  (\cref{lem:av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred}), so Milne's Lemma~3.3
   158	  (\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}) applies and gives the dichotomy: either
   159	  \(Z(f) = \emptyset\), or every point of \(Z(f)\) specialises from a point
   160	  \(z \in Z(f)\) of coheight \(1\). In the second branch, applying the
   161	  codim-\(\geq 2\) indeterminacy theorem (\cref{thm:codim_one_extension},
   162	  Milne~3.1) to such a \(z \in Z(f)\) forces \(\mathrm{coheight}(z) \geq 2\),
   163	  contradicting \(\mathrm{coheight}(z) = 1\). Hence \(Z(f) = \emptyset\).
   164	\end{proof}
   165	
   166	\section{Relations with neighbouring results}
   167	\label{sec:thm32_out_of_scope}
   168	
   169	Milne's codimension estimate and pure-codimension-one theorem are proved in
   170	\cref{chap:Albanese_CodimOneExtension} as
   171	\cref{thm:codim_one_extension} and
   172	\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}.  Their combination here is special to
   173	group-variety targets: a rational map to a general complete variety can have
   174	a nonempty codimension-two indeterminacy locus.
   175	
   176	The extension theorem feeds both the Albanese construction discussed above
   177	and the usual rigidity consequences for rational maps between abelian
   178	varieties.  Over a non-algebraically-closed field the local extension
   179	arguments remain available after suitable residue-field bookkeeping, but
   180	descent of the resulting morphism is an additional problem.

405:{"kind": "tool_result", "at": "2026-07-24T22:51:20.988556+00:00", "text": "", "tool": "Bash", "data": {"content": "     1	\chapter{Milne Theorem 3.2: Rational maps into abelian varieties}
     2	\label{chap:Albanese_Thm32RationalMapExtension}
     3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean
     4	
     5	\section{Setup and statement}
     6	\label{sec:thm32_setup}
     7	
     8	Fix an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\), a nonsingular variety \(X\) over
     9	\(\bar k\), and an abelian variety \(A\) over \(\bar k\).  Thus \(X\) is
    10	integral and smooth, while \(A\) is a complete smooth group variety.  A
    11	rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow A\) is represented by a regular
    12	morphism \(\varphi_U \colon U \to A\) on a dense open subset
    13	\(U \subseteq X\), two such pairs \((U, \varphi_U)\) and \((U', \varphi_{U'})\) being equivalent
    14	if \(\varphi_U\) and \(\varphi_{U'}\) agree on \(U \cap U'\).
    15	
    16	\begin{theorem}
    17	\leanok
    18	[Milne Theorem~3.2: a rational map from a nonsingular variety to an abelian variety extends]
    19	  \label{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends}
    20	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av}
    21	  \uses{thm:codim_one_extension, lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy, lem:av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty}
    22	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0023}
    23	
    24	  Let \(X\) be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\), let \(A\) be
    25	  an abelian variety over \(\bar k\), and let \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow A\) be a rational
    26	  map. Then \(f\) is defined on the whole of \(X\): there is a unique regular morphism
    27	  \(\widetilde f \colon X \to A\) whose restriction to some (equivalently, every) dense open
    28	  set of definition \(U \subseteq X\) of \(f\) agrees with \(\varphi_U\).
    29	\end{theorem}
    30	
    31	\begin{proof}
    32	  Let \(U\) be the maximal open subset on which \(f\) is defined, and put
    33	  \(Z=X\setminus U\).  Since a nonsingular variety is normal and \(A\) is
    34	  complete, \cref{thm:codim_one_extension} shows that every point of \(Z\)
    35	  has codimension at least two.  On the other hand,
    36	  \cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy} says that, for a rational map into a
    37	  group variety, \(Z\) is either empty or pure of codimension one.  The
    38	  second alternative is incompatible with the first conclusion, so
    39	  \(Z=\varnothing\).  Hence \(U=X\), and the representative of \(f\) on
    40	  \(U\) is the desired morphism \(\widetilde f\colon X\to A\).
    41	
    42	  If two morphisms \(X\to A\) represent \(f\), they agree on a dense open
    43	  subset of \(X\).  Their equalizer is closed because \(A\) is separated,
    44	  and it contains that dense open subset.  Since \(X\) is reduced, the two
    45	  morphisms are equal.  Thus the extension is unique.
    46	\end{proof}
    47	
    48	\begin{remark}
    49	  \label{rmk:thm32_role_of_ab}
    50	  The Auslander--Buchsbaum theorem is not needed for
    51	  \cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends}.  The codimension-one argument uses
    52	  regularity only to obtain normality and discrete valuation rings at prime
    53	  divisors; properness then supplies extensions by the valuative criterion.
    54	  It does not extend across a codimension-two locus by a depth argument.
    55	  The stronger Cohen--Macaulay consequences of Auslander--Buchsbaum in
    56	  \cref{chap:Albanese_AuslanderBuchsbaum} describe the same regular local
    57	  rings but are logically separate from Milne's proof.
    58	\end{remark}
    59	
    60	\section{Why the proof is characteristic-free}
    61	\label{sec:thm32_char_free}
    62	
    63	Both ingredients are independent of the characteristic:
    64	\begin{itemize}
    65	  \item \emph{Theorem~3.1 / codim-\(\geq 2\) extension} (\cref{thm:codim_one_extension}):
    66	    a codimension-one local ring on a normal variety is a discrete valuation
    67	    ring, and the valuative criterion of properness extends the map over that
    68	    local ring.
    69	  \item \emph{Lemma~3.3 / pure-codim-\(1\) indeterminacy for maps into a group variety}
    70	    (\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}): Milne's proof forms the difference map
    71	    \(\Phi(x, y) := \varphi(x)\,\varphi(y)^{-1} \colon X \times X \dashrightarrow A\) and
    72	    examines its pole divisors along the diagonal.  This uses the group law,
    73	    regularity, and the codimension-one support of principal divisors, none
    74	    of which imposes a characteristic restriction.
    75	\end{itemize}
    76	Consequently \cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends} holds over every algebraically closed
    77	field, in arbitrary characteristic.
    78	
    79	\section{Application to the symmetric-product Albanese map}
    80	\label{sec:thm32_application_to_a4d}
    81	
    82	Let \(C\) be a complete nonsingular curve of genus \(g>0\), let \(J\) be
    83	its Jacobian, and let \(\varphi\colon C\to A\) send a chosen point \(P\) to
    84	zero.  The symmetric map
    85	\[
    86	  (P_1,\ldots,P_g)\longmapsto
    87	  \varphi(P_1)+\cdots+\varphi(P_g)
    88	\]
    89	descends to a morphism \(\varphi^{(g)}\colon C^{(g)}\to A\).  The
    90	Abel--Jacobi morphism \(C^{(g)}\to J\) is birational, so composing
    91	\(\varphi^{(g)}\) with its rational inverse gives a rational map
    92	\(J\dashrightarrow A\).  Since \(J\) is nonsingular,
    93	\cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends} makes this map regular.  It factors
    94	\(\varphi\) through \(C\to J\), and the rigidity theorem shows that it is a
    95	homomorphism.  This is the existence step in the Albanese universal property
    96	of \(J\) proved in \cref{chap:Albanese_AlbaneseUP}.
    97	
    98	\section{Structure of the proof}
    99	\label{sec:thm32_lean_encoding}
   100	
   101	The argument separates into three elementary reductions.  Smoothness makes
   102	the abelian variety reduced; geometric irreducibility then makes it
   103	integral.  Milne's two indeterminacy results force the indeterminacy locus to
   104	be empty.  Finally, a rational map with empty indeterminacy locus has a
   105	global representative, unique because its source is reduced and its target
   106	is separated.
   107	
   108	\section{Auxiliary lemmas}
   109	\label{sec:thm32_lean_helpers}
   110	
   111	We record the reductions concerning the target and the indeterminacy locus.
   112	
   113	\begin{lemma}\leanok
   114	[A scheme smooth over a field is reduced]
   115	  \label{lem:isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}
   116	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}
   117	  Let \(A\) be a scheme over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\).  If
   118	  the structure morphism \(A\to\Spec\bar k\) is smooth, then \(A\) is
   119	  reduced.
   120	\end{lemma}
   121	\begin{proof}
   122	  An algebraically closed field is perfect.  A scheme smooth over a
   123	  perfect field is regular, since its local rings are geometrically
   124	  regular over the field.  Regular local rings are reduced, and
   125	  reducedness is local; hence \(A\) is reduced.
   126	\end{proof}
   127	
   128	\begin{lemma}\leanok
   129	[Integrality of the abelian variety]
   130	  \label{lem:av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred}
   131	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred}
   132	  \uses{lem:isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}
   133	  An abelian variety \(A\) over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\) is
   134	  integral.  Indeed, it is geometrically irreducible and smooth over
   135	  \(\bar k\), hence irreducible and reduced.
   136	\end{lemma}
   137	\begin{proof}
   138	  The spectrum of \(\bar k\) consists of one point.  Geometric
   139	  irreducibility of the structure morphism therefore implies that the
   140	  underlying topological space of \(A\) is irreducible.  By
   141	  \cref{lem:isReduced_of_smooth_over_field}, \(A\) is also reduced.  A
   142	  nonempty scheme is integral precisely when it is irreducible and
   143	  reduced, so \(A\) is integral.
   144	\end{proof}
   145	
   146	\begin{lemma}\leanok
   147	[Emptiness of the indeterminacy locus of a rational map into an abelian variety]
   148	  \label{lem:av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty}
   149	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty}
   150	  \uses{lem:av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred, lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy, thm:codim_one_extension}
   151	  For a rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow A\) from a nonsingular variety
   152	  \(X\) to an abelian variety \(A\) over an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\),
   153	  the indeterminacy locus \(Z(f)\) is empty.
   154	\end{lemma}
   155	\begin{proof}
   156	  The abelian variety \(A\) is integral
   157	  (\cref{lem:av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred}), so Milne's Lemma~3.3
   158	  (\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}) applies and gives the dichotomy: either
   159	  \(Z(f) = \emptyset\), or every point of \(Z(f)\) specialises from a point
   160	  \(z \in Z(f)\) of coheight \(1\). In the second branch, applying the
   161	  codim-\(\geq 2\) indeterminacy theorem (\cref{thm:codim_one_extension},
   162	  Milne~3.1) to such a \(z \in Z(f)\) forces \(\mathrm{coheight}(z) \geq 2\),
   163	  contradicting \(\mathrm{coheight}(z) = 1\). Hence \(Z(f) = \emptyset\).
   164	\end{proof}
   165	
   166	\section{Relations with neighbouring results}
   167	\label{sec:thm32_out_of_scope}
   168	
   169	Milne's codimension estimate and pure-codimension-one theorem are proved in
   170	\cref{chap:Albanese_CodimOneExtension} as
   171	\cref{thm:codim_one_extension} and
   172	\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}.  Their combination here is special to
   173	group-variety targets: a rational map to a general complete variety can have
   174	a nonempty codimension-two indeterminacy locus.
   175	
   176	The extension theorem feeds both the Albanese construction discussed above
   177	and the usual rigidity consequences for rational maps between abelian
   178	varieties.  Over a non-algebraically-closed field the local extension
   179	arguments remain available after suitable residue-field bookkeeping, but
   180	descent of the resulting morphism is an additional problem.
